en.headline: Police arrest eight over compensated dating scams involving HK$6.2 million
en.dek: Officers say the suspects posed as lawyers and tycoons on social media, offering large monthly payments before demanding so-called legal fees from victims.
body: Police said on Monday they had arrested eight people for allegedly operating compensated dating scams that involved 80 cases and total losses of about HK$6.2 million over the past two years.

Officers said the suspects presented fake name cards on social media platforms, pretending to be lawyers and tycoons, and offered between HK$50,000 and HK$70,000 a month to become the victims’ sugar daddies. Sixty-five percent of the victims were women, and more than half worked in the services trade or as office workers. The largest single loss was HK$480,000. All transactions were conducted online and the victims never met the scammers in person.

Victims were required to pay a so-called legal fee before they could receive the promised money, police said. The arrests were made last week in an operation codenamed Tight Net. Superintendent Cheung Hau-yee said the public should verify any claimed professional credentials directly with the relevant firm rather than relying on cards sent by strangers. The ringleader and a core member were charged with money laundering and conspiracy to defraud and remain in custody; the others were released on bail.

zh.headline: 警方拘八人涉援交詐騙涉款620萬元
zh.dek: 疑犯在社交平台出示假名片，自稱律師或富商，承諾每月支付數萬元後向事主索取所謂律師費。
body: 警方周一表示，已拘捕八人，涉嫌在過去兩年內經營援交詐騙，涉及80宗案件，總損失約620萬元。
警方指，疑犯在社交平台出示假名片，偽稱律師及富商，向事主提出每月支付5萬至7萬元作為「包養」條件。65%事主為女性，逾半從事服務業或任文職。單宗最高損失48萬元。所有交易均在網上進行，事主從未與疑犯見面。
事主須先支付所謂律師費才能收取款項。行動代號「緊網」，於上周進行。總督察張巧儀呼籲市民直接向相關律師行核實身份，切勿輕信陌生人傳來的名片。主腦及核心成員被控洗黑錢及串謀詐騙，仍被扣押，其餘獲准保釋。
